core_phrases.irish: Conas a théann mé go dtí an aerfort?
core_phrases.english: How do I get to the airport?
core_phrases.pronunciation_tip: Kun-us a hayn may go dee an air-fort

core_phrases.irish: An bhfuil taxi ag fanacht linn?
core_phrases.english: Is the taxi waiting for us?
core_phrases.pronunciation_tip: An wil taxi eg fahn-ukht lin

core_phrases.irish: Ar mhaith leat ticéad ar an traein?
core_phrases.english: Would you like a ticket on the train?
core_phrases.pronunciation_tip: Air wuh lat tick-ayd er an trayn

grammar_rule.title: Asking for Directions
grammar_rule.explanation: Use 'Cá bhfuil' (Where is) to ask for locations. Example: Cá bhfuil an bialann? (Where is the restaurant?)

pronunciation_notes: Practice the 'bh' sound which is like a 'v' sound in English.
Pay attention to the slender 't' and 'd' sounds in Irish.
Focus on the stress patterns in longer phrases.

mini_task.instruction: Imagine you are a tourist asking for directions in a new city. Record yourself asking how to get to the nearest bus stop.
prompts: Ask 'Cá bhfuil an stáisiún bus is cóngarach?' (Where is the nearest bus station?)
Express gratitude in Irish after receiving directions.
